correctness.rationale: For a spanning two-factor, every lifted vertex has degree two in its pullback; because the universal cover is a tree, each component is a bi-infinite line. Deck transformations preserve the pullback, and spanning makes the root coverage probability one. Inspection of Proposition 4.1 shows the finite Hamiltonian cycle is used only to obtain such a full invariant line ensemble; the subsequent labeling and von Neumann-dimension argument therefore carries over unchanged. Section 4.3 separately proves that the spectral bottom is strictly below the least Dirichlet value. Hence the bottom cannot be an eigenvalue or an isolated spectral point, and Theorem 1.2 forces a nonempty band with purely absolutely continuous interior. Quantifiers, Dirichlet exceptional values, and the (C1) scope are preserved.

value.rationale: The source itself isolates nonemptiness of the continuous spectrum as a separate problem and singles out the Petersen graph as a non-Hamiltonian regular base. The two-factor criterion is a natural structural weakening that applies to genuinely anisotropic, edge-dependent quantum data on non-Hamiltonian bases, which the source's alternate Hamiltonian-cover workaround does not preserve. It therefore enlarges the usable class of finite quantum graphs rather than evaluating an arbitrary parameter slice.
